newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FUN IN BRUSSELS: RAIL-BIKING IN THE ARDENNES.
newsitem.headline: FUN IN BRUSSELS: RAIL-BIKING IN THE ARDENNES.

text.p: Are you a city-dweller who finds urban life somewhat claustrophobic, would like a day out in the countryside, but need the inspiration to actually get out of the metropolis at week-ends?
Maybe that inspiration might just come from the obscure sounding activity of rail-biking.
Rail-biking? Imagine a western film with cowboys on old rail-carts desperately pumping handles to move along tracks.
A rail-bike is simply a bicycle that is attached to an old railway by small metalic wheels. They are ridden by two people, with room for two more as passengers.
In Les Draisines de la Molignee, an hour's drive south of Brussels near the village of Falaen in the Ardennes, rail enthusiast Paul Arnould has turned rail-biking into a leisure business.
Two routes are available: one of an hour in length, the other of an hour-and-a-half. It's recommended to try both.

The first and shorter track starts out with a downhill ride for about 15 minutes. At this point it is easy to picture yourself as someone in an old western; I was half expecting to round the corner and find a helpless damsel tied to the track.

The ride is smooth, and you pass downhill through a tunnel with a small valley on either side. If you look carefully, you can see the ancient ruins of the medieval castle of Montaigle. The castle was built in the early fourteenth century and destroyed not much later by troops of French King Henri II.
At the bottom of the track, one arrives at an ancient charcoal oven and a modern quarry. Then, after a short break, it's time for the gentle slog back up to the start.
The other route starts uphill and leads to the disused station of Maretsou.
Arnould claims to have first had the idea for rail-bikes over twenty years ago.
His initial attempts to establish rail-biking were unsuccessful, but in 1993, he managed to get his hands on a stretch of old track in the Namur province of southern Belgium.
By then rail-biking had been established in France and Sweden, but Belgium, with formerly the densest rail network in the world, had been neglected.
Arnould is currently in the process of extending both tracks by a further 4 kms.

As for the line itself, it was originally built between 1870-90 linking Charleroi and the Ardennes, largely to transporte coal and rail sleepers made from the woods in the Ardennes. It was of strategic importance in both world wars, but it proved of little use thereafter and was closed in the 1960s.
